cards.title: Lantern queue
cards.essence: A lantern queue keeps arrival order and lets readers skip ahead by lit markers.
propositions: Readers skip ahead by following lit markers.
cards.intuition: Like lamp posts along a road: you can walk to the next lamp without counting stones.
confusions: Unlike an index, markers are placed by count, not by key.

flashcards.q: What order does a lantern queue keep?
How does a reader skip ahead?
flashcards.a: By jumping to a lit marker.

source_quotes: A lantern queue keeps every item in arrival order but lets a reader skip ahead by lit markers.

cards.title: Lit marker memory cost
cards.essence: Each lit marker costs one extra word, one marker per eight items.
propositions: A writer lights a marker every eight items.
Each marker costs one word of memory; 800 items carry 100 markers.

flashcards.q: How often is a marker lit?
How many markers do 800 items carry?

source_quotes: A writer lights a marker every eight items.
so a queue of 800 items carries 100 markers
